## Criteria (the build must meet every line)
1. packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file named in order and prints <file>:<line>: <error> for each bad row, as for one file before
2. A file named - is read from stdin and reported as -; a second - is a usage error (exit 2)
3. Exit 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read (error on stderr, other files still checked and reported)
4. lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged
5. node:test tests cover two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via - (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones, two - arguments and no arguments; the package README documents the usage
6. The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head

## Steps
1. Read packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js, packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js, packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js, packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js and packages/jsonl-lint/README.md. Do not edit packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js at all.
2. Rewrite packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js (zero dependencies, plain ES module):
   - Take all of process.argv.slice(2) as files. If there are none, print a usage line (e.g. `usage: jsonl-lint <file> [<file> ...]`) to stderr and exit 2.
   - Before reading anything, if `-` appears more than once, print a usage error to stderr and exit 2 without reading stdin (so it never blocks waiting on input) and without printing any row output.
   - Process files in the order given. For `-`, read stdin fully (e.g. readFileSync(0, 'utf8')) and use `-` as the prefix. For other names, readFileSync(name, 'utf8'); the prefix is the argument exactly as given.
   - For each bad row print `<file>:<line>: <error>` to stdout exactly as the single-file version did (same newline-stripping of the error message).
   - If a file can't be read, print `jsonl-lint: cannot read <file>: <message>` to stderr, remember the failure, and continue with the remaining files.
   - Exit 2 if any file couldn't be read; otherwise 1 if any bad row was found in any file; otherwise 0.
   - Keep the existing single-file behaviour and output identical so the existing tests still pass.
3. Extend packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js with node:test tests (spawnSync the bin; pass stdin with the `input` option) for: two clean files (exit 0, no stdout/stderr); one bad file among several clean ones (exit 1, only that file's rows printed, prefixed with its path); stdin via `-` clean (exit 0) and bad (exit 1, lines prefixed `-:`); a missing file among good ones, including one with a bad row after the missing one (exit 2, stderr names the missing file, other files' bad rows still on stdout); two `-` arguments (exit 2, stderr non-empty, no stdout); no arguments (exit 2, usage on stderr). Also assert output order follows argument order when two files are bad.
4. Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md: usage `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...]`, `-` means stdin (reported as `-`, only once), files checked in order, and the exit codes 0/1/2 as in criterion 3 (unreadable files reported on stderr while the rest are still checked).
5. Run `npm test` at the repository root and make it pass.
6. Commit and open exactly one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body contains the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`. Wait for the `test` workflow on the PR head to finish; if it fails, fix it and push to the same PR until it is green.
result.verifier:
Check out the PR head of the single PR for https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104 and run `npm ci` at the repository root. Below, BIN = packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js. Make a scratch dir with: a.jsonl = `{"a":1}\n`, b.jsonl = `{"b":2}\n\n{"c":3}\n`, bad.jsonl = `{"x":1}\n{oops}\n{"torn":`, bad2.jsonl = `{nope}\n`. Run every command with a timeout (e.g. `timeout 10`) and record stdout, stderr and exit status.

## Check 1 — multi-file, in order, `<file>:<line>: <error>`
Run `node BIN a.jsonl bad.jsonl b.jsonl bad2.jsonl`. Also run `node BIN bad.jsonl` alone and compute expected output with `node -e` importing lint from packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js.
PASS: multi-file stdout is exactly the lines for bad.jsonl (`bad.jsonl:2: ...`, `bad.jsonl:3: ...`) followed by `bad2.jsonl:1: ...`, in that order, each `<file>:<line>: <error>` with the argument as given and the error equal to lint()'s message; the bad.jsonl lines are identical to the single-file run; nothing printed for clean files.
FAIL: any file skipped, wrong order, wrong prefix/format, or output differing from the single-file format.

## Check 2 — `-` is stdin, reported as `-`; second `-` is exit 2
Run `printf '{"a":1}\n{bad}\n' | node BIN -`, `printf '{"a":1}\n' | node BIN a.jsonl - b.jsonl`, and `printf '{bad}\n' | node BIN - -` and `node BIN - - < /dev/null`.
PASS: first prints `-:2: <error>` and exits 1; second exits 0 with no stdout; both `- -` runs exit 2 (within the timeout).
FAIL: stdin not read, prefix not `-`, or a second `-` not giving exit 2.

## Check 3 — exit codes and unreadable files
Run: `node BIN a.jsonl b.jsonl` (expect 0, no stdout); `node BIN a.jsonl bad.jsonl` (expect 1); `node BIN` (expect 2, stderr non-empty); `node BIN a.jsonl missing.jsonl bad2.jsonl` (expect 2).
PASS: statuses are 0, 1, 2, 2; the no-argument and missing-file runs write an error to stderr; the missing-file run still prints `bad2.jsonl:1: ...` on stdout and stderr names missing.jsonl.
FAIL: any other status, no stderr message, or files after the missing one not checked/reported.

## Check 4 — lint(text) unchanged
Run `git diff $(git merge-base HEAD origin/$(gh pr view <PR> --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName)) HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` and run `node --test packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js`.
PASS: the diff shows no change to the lint function (empty diff) and lint tests pass.
FAIL: the lint function body or signature changed, or lint tests fail.

## Check 5 — tests cover the cases; README documents usage
Read packages/jsonl-lint/test/*.test.js and run `node --test` in packages/jsonl-lint.
PASS: tests pass and there are node:test tests for each of: two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via `-` clean, stdin via `-` bad, a missing file among good ones, two `-` arguments, no arguments; and packages/jsonl-lint/README.md documents multi-file usage (`<file> [<file> ...]` or equivalent) and `-` for stdin.
FAIL: any listed case lacks a test, tests fail, or the README lacks the multi-file/`-` usage.

## Check 6 — one PR, body, green
Run `gh pr list --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test --state all --search 104`, `gh pr view <PR> --json body,headRefOid`, `gh pr checks <PR>`, and `npm test` at the repository root on the PR head.
PASS: exactly one PR for this issue; its body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`; `npm test` exits 0; the `test` workflow run for the head commit concluded success.
FAIL: multiple PRs, missing closing line, npm test failing, or the workflow failing/missing/not finished for the head commit.

## Advisory
- Note (not a fail condition) whether `- -` exits 2 without blocking on stdin when stdin is left open (try without redirect under `timeout 5`).
- Note whether the README exit-code section reflects the multi-file rules.
